(a) Give an account of the creation of man and woman according to Genesis 2. [9 marks]
(b) State three lessons that Christians can learn from this account. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the LORD God formed man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life
2 marks: man was placed in the garden of Eden to till and keep it, with the command not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
2 marks: God said it was not good for man to be alone; the animals were brought and the man named them, but no fit helper was found
3 marks: God caused a deep sleep, took a rib and made woman; man said 'bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh'; a man leaves his parents and cleaves to his wife
6 marks: any three lessons, 2 marks each - God is the source of life; human dignity; work is God-given; obedience to God; marriage is God's plan; companionship
questions.explanation: Model answer: God formed man from dust and breathed life into him, set him in Eden to till and keep it and forbade him the tree of knowledge. Seeing that man should not be alone, God brought the animals for naming, then made woman from his rib while he slept; the man welcomed her as bone of his bones. The account teaches that life comes from God, that work and marriage are part of His plan and that obedience is required.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the call of Moses at the burning bush. [10 marks]
(b) Mention two qualities of leadership shown by Moses in his response to the call. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Moses kept Jethro's flock and came to Horeb, the mountain of God; the bush burned but was not consumed
2 marks: God called 'Moses, Moses', told him to remove his shoes, and identified Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
2 marks: God had seen the affliction of His people and was sending Moses to Pharaoh to bring them out
2 marks: Moses' objections - 'Who am I?'; asked God's name: 'I AM WHO I AM'
2 marks: signs given - rod into serpent, leprous hand; Moses slow of speech, Aaron appointed spokesman
3 marks: first quality - humility (felt unworthy) or dependence on God
2 marks: second quality - obedience/willingness after assurance, or concern for his people
questions.explanation: Model answer: While keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses saw a bush burning without being consumed. God called him, told him to remove his shoes and revealed Himself as the God of the fathers who had seen Israel's suffering and was sending him to Pharaoh. Moses objected that he was unworthy and slow of speech; God gave His name, signs and Aaron as spokesman. Moses showed humility and, in the end, obedience.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate how Deborah led Israel to victory over Sisera. [10 marks]
(b) What lessons can a Nigerian woman leader learn from Deborah? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Israel did evil and was oppressed for twenty years by Jabin of Hazor whose commander Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots
2 marks: Deborah, a prophetess judging Israel, summoned Barak and commanded him to gather 10,000 men of Naphtali and Zebulun at Mount Tabor
2 marks: Barak would go only if Deborah went; she agreed but said the glory would go to a woman
2 marks: the LORD routed Sisera and his chariots; Barak pursued and the army fell
2 marks: Sisera fled to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, who killed him with a tent peg
5 marks: any lessons (3 + 2) - courage, faith in God, decisiveness, wisdom in judgment, willingness to work with others
questions.explanation: Model answer: Oppressed by Jabin and his general Sisera, Israel cried to the LORD. Deborah sent for Barak and ordered him to gather ten thousand men at Tabor; he insisted she accompany him, and she foretold that a woman would get the glory. The LORD routed Sisera's chariots, and Jael killed Sisera in her tent. A woman leader learns courage, faith and wise cooperation.

questions.stem:
(a) How did Eli fail in his responsibility as a parent? [8 marks]
(b) What were the consequences of this failure? [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: his sons Hophni and Phinehas were worthless men who did not know the LORD
2 marks: they took the sacrificial meat by force before the fat was burnt, treating the offering with contempt
2 marks: they lay with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting
2 marks: Eli only rebuked them mildly and did not restrain them; he honoured his sons above God
2 marks: a man of God and Samuel's vision foretold judgment on Eli's house
3 marks: Israel defeated by the Philistines; ark captured; Hophni and Phinehas killed on the same day
2 marks: Eli fell and broke his neck; Phinehas' wife died after naming her son Ichabod
questions.explanation: Model answer: Eli's sons abused the sacrifices and lay with the women serving at the sanctuary, yet Eli gave only a weak rebuke and did not restrain them. God declared judgment through a man of God and through Samuel. In the battle with the Philistines the ark was taken and both sons died; Eli fell and broke his neck, and Phinehas' wife named her son Ichabod.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how Saul disobeyed God in the war against the Amalekites. [8 marks]
(b) State the consequences of his disobedience. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Samuel commanded Saul to utterly destroy Amalek, people and animals
2 marks: Saul defeated Amalek but spared Agag and the best of the sheep, oxen and other good things
2 marks: Saul claimed he had obeyed and that the people kept the animals for sacrifice
2 marks: Samuel declared that to obey is better than sacrifice and rebellion is like divination
2 marks: God rejected Saul as king
2 marks: the Spirit of the LORD departed and an evil spirit tormented him
3 marks: defeat and death on Mount Gilboa with his sons; disgrace of his body at Beth-shan
questions.explanation: Model answer: Told to destroy Amalek completely, Saul spared King Agag and the best of the livestock and then blamed the people, claiming the animals were for sacrifice. Samuel replied that obedience is better than sacrifice. God rejected Saul; the Spirit departed and an evil spirit troubled him; he finally died with his sons on Gilboa and his body was hung on the wall of Beth-shan.

questions.topic: The unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam
questions.stem:
(a) In what ways did Solomon's decisions contribute to the division of the kingdom? [8 marks]
(b) How did Rehoboam's decision at Shechem lead to the split? [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Solomon used forced labour for his building projects, burdening the people
2 marks: he married many foreign wives
2 marks: they turned his heart to other gods such as Ashtoreth, Milcom and Chemosh, and he built high places for them
2 marks: God declared that He would tear the kingdom from his son, leaving one tribe for David's sake
2 marks: Israel asked Rehoboam at Shechem to lighten the heavy yoke of Solomon
2 marks: he rejected the old men's advice and followed the young men
3 marks: his harsh reply ('scorpions'); the northern tribes rebelled, stoned Adoram, made Jeroboam king; only Judah followed the house of David
questions.explanation: Model answer: Solomon's forced labour and heavy burdens, his many foreign wives and his worship of their gods brought God's sentence that the kingdom would be torn from his son. At Shechem the people begged Rehoboam to lighten the yoke; he spurned the elders and threatened them with scorpions, so the northern tribes rebelled, stoned Adoram and made Jeroboam king, leaving only Judah to the house of David.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the contest between Elijah and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. [10 marks]
(b) What lessons does the story teach Christians today? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Elijah gathered the people and the 450 prophets of Baal; he challenged the people to stop limping between two opinions
2 marks: two bulls were prepared; the god who answered by fire would be God
2 marks: Baal's prophets called from morning to noon, danced and cut themselves; Elijah mocked them; no answer
2 marks: Elijah repaired the altar with twelve stones, made a trench and had water poured over the offering three times
2 marks: he prayed; fire fell and consumed everything; the people cried 'The LORD, he is God'; the prophets of Baal were killed at the Kishon
5 marks: any lessons (3 + 2) - God alone is supreme; avoid divided loyalty; courage to stand for truth; power of prayer; God answers faith
questions.explanation: Model answer: Elijah called Israel and the 450 prophets of Baal to Carmel and proposed that the god who answered by fire was God. Baal's prophets cried and cut themselves all day without answer. Elijah rebuilt the altar with twelve stones, drenched the offering and prayed; fire fell and consumed it all, the people confessed the LORD, and Baal's prophets were slain. God alone is supreme, and believers must not waver.

questions.topic: Response to the state of the nation
questions.stem:
(a) Show how Nehemiah responded to the news of the condition of Jerusalem. [9 marks]
(b) Mention three ways a Nigerian citizen can show concern for the nation. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: he wept, mourned, fasted and prayed, confessing the sins of Israel
2 marks: he asked King Artaxerxes for permission and letters to go and rebuild the city
2 marks: he inspected the walls secretly at night and encouraged the people to rebuild
3 marks: he resisted the mockery and threats of Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem; he armed the builders, with half working and half on guard
6 marks: any three, 2 marks each - prayer for the nation; honest work and payment of taxes; obedience to laws; voting and active participation; volunteering for community development; opposing corruption
questions.explanation: Model answer: Nehemiah wept, fasted and prayed when he heard that the wall of Jerusalem was broken. He obtained the king's permission and letters, inspected the walls at night, rallied the people, and answered the mockery and threats of Sanballat and Tobiah by arming the builders. A Nigerian can show similar concern by praying, working honestly, obeying laws and joining in community development.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate how Daniel was delivered from the lions' den. [10 marks]
(b) State two lessons Christians can learn from Daniel's faith. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Darius set Daniel over the presidents and satraps; jealous officials could find no fault in him except concerning his God
2 marks: they persuaded the king to sign an ordinance that for thirty days no one should petition any god or man except the king
2 marks: Daniel continued to pray three times a day with his windows open towards Jerusalem
2 marks: he was thrown into the den; the king fasted and came early; Daniel said God sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths
2 marks: Daniel was taken up unhurt; his accusers were cast in and destroyed; Darius decreed that men should fear Daniel's God
3 marks: first lesson - faithfulness in prayer whatever the cost
2 marks: second lesson - God delivers those who trust Him / integrity at work
questions.explanation: Model answer: Jealous officials, unable to fault Daniel, tricked Darius into decreeing that for thirty days no one should pray except to the king. Daniel kept praying three times daily towards Jerusalem and was thrown to the lions. God's angel shut their mouths; Daniel emerged unharmed, his accusers were destroyed and Darius honoured Daniel's God. Christians learn steadfastness in prayer and trust in God's power.

questions.topic: True religion and social justice - Amos
questions.stem:
(a) Discuss the social evils which Amos condemned in Israel. [10 marks]
(b) What according to Amos does God require instead of empty worship? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: selling the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of shoes
2 marks: trampling the head of the poor and turning aside the afflicted
2 marks: luxury and oppression by the rich women of Samaria (cows of Bashan)
2 marks: cheating in trade - making the ephah small and the shekel great, false balances, selling refuse of the wheat
2 marks: perverting justice in the gate and taking bribes; sexual immorality
5 marks: justice rolling down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream; seeking God and doing good rather than feasts and offerings
questions.explanation: Model answer: Amos condemned Israel for selling the needy for a pair of sandals, crushing the poor, the luxury of the 'cows of Bashan', dishonest trading with false measures and the corruption of justice. God rejected their feasts and offerings and demanded that justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.

questions.stem:
(a) Using Matthew's Gospel, narrate what happened when Jesus came to John at the Jordan. [9 marks]
(b) Why did Jesus, who was without sin, submit to baptism? Give three reasons. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptised by John
2 marks: John would have prevented him, saying 'I need to be baptised by you'
2 marks: Jesus said 'Let it be so now; for thus it is fitting for us to fulfil all righteousness'
3 marks: when he came up from the water the heavens opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and a voice said 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased'
6 marks: any three, 2 marks each - to fulfil all righteousness; to identify with sinners; to set an example; to be revealed/anointed for his ministry; to receive God's approval
questions.explanation: Model answer: Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan. John protested that he needed to be baptised by Jesus, but Jesus insisted, to fulfil all righteousness. As he came up from the water the heavens opened, the Spirit descended like a dove and the Father declared him His beloved Son. He was baptised to fulfil righteousness, identify with sinners, set an example and be revealed for his mission.

questions.stem:
(a) Relate how Jesus overcame each of the three temptations in Matthew 4:1-11. [9 marks]
(b) Suggest three ways in which young Christians can resist temptation today. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: after fasting forty days, Jesus was tempted to turn stones into bread; he replied that man shall not live by bread alone but by every word from God
3 marks: on the pinnacle of the temple he was tempted to throw himself down; he replied 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God'
3 marks: on a high mountain he was offered the kingdoms of the world for worship; he replied 'Begone, Satan!... him only shall you serve'; the devil left and angels ministered
6 marks: any three, 2 marks each - knowledge and use of Scripture; prayer and fasting; reliance on the Holy Spirit; avoiding occasions of sin; good company/fellowship; firm resolve to obey God
questions.explanation: Model answer: After fasting forty days, Jesus was tempted to turn stones into bread, to throw himself from the temple and to worship Satan for the world's kingdoms. Each time he answered with Scripture, and the devil left him. Christians overcome temptation through Scripture, prayer, the help of the Spirit and avoiding situations of sin.

questions.topic: The Call and Demands of Discipleship
questions.stem:
(a) Discuss the demands of discipleship as taught by Jesus in Luke 9:57-62 and Luke 14:25-33. [10 marks]
(b) Give two reasons why some Christians today find these demands difficult. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a disciple must be ready for hardship - 'the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head'
2 marks: the kingdom comes before family duties - 'Leave the dead to bury their own dead'
2 marks: no turning back - 'No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God'
2 marks: love for Jesus must exceed love for family and even one's own life; bearing one's cross
2 marks: counting the cost (tower builder, king going to war) and renouncing all that one has
3 marks: first reason - love of wealth and comfort / materialism
2 marks: second reason - family pressure, fear of persecution or lack of commitment
questions.explanation: Model answer: Jesus warned would-be followers that discipleship means homelessness and hardship, putting the kingdom before family obligations and never looking back. In Luke 14 he required greater love for him than for family, carrying one's cross, counting the cost like a builder or a king, and renouncing all. Many find this hard because of love of comfort and wealth, family pressure and fear of suffering.

questions.stem:
(a) Narrate the parable of the unforgiving servant. [10 marks]
(b) State two lessons of the parable for Christians. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Peter asked whether to forgive seven times; Jesus said seventy times seven
2 marks: a king settled accounts with a servant who owed ten thousand talents and could not pay
2 marks: the servant begged for patience and the king, moved with pity, forgave the whole debt
2 marks: the servant seized a fellow servant who owed a hundred denarii and threw him into prison
2 marks: the king, told by other servants, called him wicked and delivered him to the jailers until he paid all
3 marks: first lesson - those forgiven by God must forgive others without limit
2 marks: second lesson - God will not forgive the unforgiving / forgive from the heart
questions.explanation: Model answer: Answering Peter, Jesus told of a king who forgave a servant ten thousand talents. That servant then jailed a fellow servant over a hundred denarii; the king summoned him, condemned his lack of mercy and handed him to the jailers. So the Father treats those who do not forgive from the heart. Christians must forgive generously because they have been forgiven much.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the experience of Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane. [10 marks]
(b) What lessons can Christians learn from the event? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Jesus took Peter, James and John and began to be sorrowful and troubled
2 marks: he prayed 'My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as thou wilt'
2 marks: he found the disciples sleeping three times and warned them to watch and pray
2 marks: Judas came with a crowd from the chief priests and betrayed him with a kiss
2 marks: a disciple cut off the ear of the high priest's slave; Jesus rebuked him; the disciples forsook him and fled
5 marks: any lessons (3 + 2) - submission to God's will; importance of prayer in crisis; watchfulness; non-violence; loyalty
questions.explanation: Model answer: In Gethsemane Jesus, deeply distressed, took Peter, James and John and prayed that the cup might pass, yet submitted to the Father's will. Three times he found them asleep. Judas arrived with an armed crowd and kissed him; when a disciple struck the high priest's slave, Jesus forbade violence, and all the disciples fled. Christians learn to pray, submit to God and remain watchful and loyal.

questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of the appearance of the risen Jesus to the two disciples on the road to Emmaus. [10 marks]
(b) State the importance of the resurrection for Christians. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: two disciples, one named Cleopas, were going to Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem, discussing the events
2 marks: Jesus drew near but their eyes were kept from recognising him; they told him of the crucifixion and the empty tomb
2 marks: he called them foolish and slow of heart and interpreted the Scriptures concerning himself
2 marks: they urged him to stay; at table he took bread, blessed and broke it, and their eyes were opened; he vanished
2 marks: 'Did not our hearts burn within us?'; they returned to Jerusalem and reported to the eleven
5 marks: any (3 + 2) - proves Jesus is Son of God; victory over death; hope of eternal life; foundation of Christian faith; assurance of forgiveness
questions.explanation: Model answer: Two disciples, one called Cleopas, walking to Emmaus, were joined by the risen Jesus whom they did not recognise. He explained from the Scriptures why the Christ had to suffer. At supper he broke bread and they knew him; he vanished, and they hurried back to tell the eleven. The resurrection confirms Jesus as Lord, conquers death and gives believers hope of eternal life.

questions.stem:
(a) What happened to the apostles and to the crowd in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost? [10 marks]
(b) In what two ways did the coming of the Holy Spirit change the apostles? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the apostles were together in one place; a sound like a rushing mighty wind filled the house
2 marks: tongues as of fire rested on each; they were filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke in other tongues
2 marks: devout Jews from every nation heard them in their own languages; some mocked that they were full of new wine
2 marks: Peter preached, quoting Joel, proclaiming Jesus crucified and raised as Lord and Christ
2 marks: the people were cut to the heart; Peter called them to repent and be baptised; about three thousand were added
3 marks: first effect - boldness to preach
2 marks: second effect - power to speak in tongues/perform signs, or unity and fellowship
questions.explanation: Model answer: At Pentecost the apostles heard a sound like a mighty wind, saw tongues as of fire and, filled with the Spirit, spoke in other languages understood by Jews from many nations. Some mocked them as drunk, but Peter explained, citing Joel, that God had raised Jesus and poured out the Spirit; he called for repentance and baptism, and about three thousand believed. The Spirit made the apostles bold and gave them power.

questions.stem:
(a) Give an account of the imprisonment and release of the apostles in Acts 5:17-42. [10 marks]
(b) What can Christians learn from the attitude of the apostles to persecution? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: filled with jealousy, the high priest and Sadducees arrested the apostles and put them in the common prison
2 marks: an angel opened the doors at night and told them to speak in the temple; they taught there at daybreak
2 marks: they were brought before the council; Peter declared 'We must obey God rather than men'
2 marks: the council wanted to kill them, but Gamaliel advised that if the work was of God it could not be overthrown
2 marks: they were beaten, charged not to speak in Jesus' name and released; they rejoiced and kept preaching daily
5 marks: any (3 + 2) - courage; obedience to God above men; joy in suffering; perseverance; reliance on God's help
questions.explanation: Model answer: Jealous temple leaders jailed the apostles, but an angel freed them and sent them to preach in the temple. Brought before the council, Peter insisted that they must obey God rather than men. Gamaliel urged caution, so they were flogged and released; they rejoiced to suffer for the Name and preached daily. Christians learn courage, obedience to God and joy under persecution.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain James' teaching on faith and works. [10 marks]
(b) Show how a Christian student can put this teaching into practice. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: faith without works is dead; mere words to a needy brother ('go in peace, be warmed') are useless
2 marks: faith is shown by works - 'I by my works will show you my faith'
2 marks: even the demons believe and shudder; belief alone is not enough
2 marks: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith was completed by works
2 marks: Rahab was justified by works when she received the messengers; be doers of the word, not hearers only
5 marks: any (3 + 2) - helping needy classmates; honesty in examinations; obeying school rules; caring for the sick and orphans; serving in community projects
questions.explanation: Model answer: James taught that faith without works is dead: telling a hungry brother to be warm and fed without helping him is worthless, and even demons believe. Abraham's offering of Isaac and Rahab's welcome of the spies show faith completed by action, so believers must be doers of the word. A student practises this by helping the needy, being honest in examinations and serving others.

questions.stem:
(a) Outline the instructions of 1 Peter 2:13-17 on the Christian's relationship with civil authority. [9 marks]
(b) Suggest three ways a Christian can practise these instructions in Nigeria today. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: be subject for the Lord's sake to every human institution, the emperor as supreme and governors
2 marks: governors are sent to punish wrongdoers and praise those who do right
2 marks: by doing right Christians should silence the ignorance of foolish men
3 marks: live as free men without using freedom as a pretext for evil; honour all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honour the emperor
6 marks: any three, 2 marks each - obeying laws; paying taxes; voting and taking part in elections; respecting leaders; avoiding corruption; praying for the nation
questions.explanation: Model answer: Peter told believers to submit to every human authority for the Lord's sake because rulers punish wrong and praise right, to silence critics by good conduct, to use freedom responsibly and to honour all, love the brotherhood, fear God and honour the emperor. A Nigerian Christian obeys the law, pays taxes, votes, respects leaders and avoids corruption.
